help.title: Veritas: a fast, permissionless prediction market
help.sub: Hourly markets on crypto prices. Anyone can open one, anyone can trade — and settlement needs no one's permission: the first Pyth price printed after expiry decides.
help.v1Title: Open a market with just over 1 USDT
help.v1: No listing review, no gatekeeper. Seed a market with a little over 1 USDT of collateral and it is live.
help.v2: Which side redeems is decided by the first price Pyth prints after expiry — a rule anyone can verify on-chain, not a person you have to trust.
help.v3: Every trade pays 0.3% on the way in and 0.3% on the way out. The protocol takes none of it — all of it goes to the makers who were in the pool.
help.risk: Making markets is not free money. When the price moves, better-informed traders trade against you first — that adverse-selection loss (LVR) is the real cost of providing liquidity, and fees only partly offset it. Veritas shrinks the risk rather than erasing it: a maker's exposure winds down automatically as expiry approaches. And if settlement data fails to arrive in time, the market is voided and every token redeems at 0.5 USDT, instead of anyone being paid out on a stale price.
help.a1Title: pm-AMM: liquidity that releases over time
help.a1: Veritas prices markets with a pm-AMM curve: the YES price comes from the balance between the two reserve sides, not from an order book. The pool's effective depth is not constant — it decays with the square root of the time remaining, so as expiry approaches, reserves are steadily released back to makers as claimable balances instead of staying locked in the pool. A maker can claim what was released, merge it back into full sets, and re-add it — recycling the same capital instead of topping up with new money. The practical effect: the closer a market gets to settlement, the less a maker has at risk, which is exactly when standing on the wrong side of the final price hurts most.
help.a2Title: Settlement: only the first print counts
help.a2: Once a market expires, anyone can settle it by posting the market's Pyth price update. The contract accepts one reading and one only: the first print timestamped at or after expiry, proven on-chain by checking that the previous print still fell before expiry. Nobody can shop for a friendlier later price. Two fallback rules keep it honest: if that first print lands more than 10 seconds after expiry, the data is treated as too stale to trust and the market is voided rather than settled; and if nobody settles within 48 hours, anyone can void it. A voided market is a clean refund — Yes and No both redeem at 0.5 USDT per token.
help.footnote: Veritas currently runs on Solana Devnet — a demo environment, and no real funds are involved.
help.quickTitle: New here? Start in three steps
help.q1: Use Phantom or any Solana wallet and switch its network to Devnet — Veritas runs on the test network, so nothing here touches real funds.
help.q2: Devnet SOL pays the transaction fees — get it free from the official Solana faucet. Test USDT is what you trade with: connect your wallet and claim 100 of it right here, once a day.
help.q2Cooldown: Already claimed today — come back tomorrow
help.q3: Open any live market, pick YES or NO, and confirm. Your position shows up under Me, and after settlement you redeem at 1:1 on the same market page.
help.ex1: Target 73,741; the first print after expiry reads 73,802 — above the target, so YES redeems 1:1 and NO expires worthless.
help.ex2: Same target, but the first print lands 12 seconds after expiry — too stale to trust, so the market is voided instead and every token redeems at 0.5 USDT.

errors.notOpen: Market is not open. Wait until it is live, or void it after the window.
errors.cannotRedeem: Market is not resolved or voided. Submit settlement or wait.
errors.cannotMerge: Market is not in a state that allows merge or LP withdrawal. Use a live, resolved, or voided market.
errors.expired: Market has expired. Trading is closed; submit settlement if the window is open.
errors.outsideWindow: Outside the 48-hour settlement window. Void the market instead.
errors.invalidAmount: Amount or expiry is invalid. Seed must be > 1 USDT and expiry in the future.
errors.notEnoughTokens: Insufficient token balance. Reduce size or fund the account.
errors.emptyPool: Pool reserves are empty. This market cannot trade.
errors.slippage: Output is below slippage protection. Increase slippage or reduce size.
errors.lpZero: LP amount must be greater than zero.
errors.wrongMint: Mint does not belong to this market. Use the market's YES or NO mint.
errors.onlyWinner: Only the redeeming side can be redeemed. Switch sides, or use the void rules.
errors.invalidPrice: On-chain price is out of range. Retry; if it persists the pool is too skewed.
errors.invalidLiquidity: Liquidity math rejected the size. Reduce the LP amount.
errors.invalidBudget: Seed budget is invalid. Increase the seed above 1 USDT.
errors.notFirstPrint: This Pyth print is not the first after expiry. Fetch a later print and retry.
errors.exponentMismatch: Pyth exponent does not match this market. Use the feed preset recorded on the market.
errors.accountMissing: Account not found. Confirm the address and network.
errors.badAddress: Program ID or mint is not a valid public key. Reset Settings.
errors.noSol: Not enough SOL for fees. Airdrop or transfer SOL.
errors.rpcAuth: RPC rejected the request. Check the API key.
errors.txFailed: Transaction failed. Retry, or inspect logs on the explorer.
errors.mintNotFound: Collateral mint not found. Check Settings.
errors.decode: On-chain data could not be read. Retry, or check the program address in Settings.
errors.pythFetch: Could not get the price print from Pyth Hermes.
errors.pythNoPrint: No first Pyth print after expiry is available yet. Wait for the next publish, then retry.
